bhedābheda-vāda
(‘the doctrine of difference and non-difference’)
------------------------------------------
One of the important concepts discussed by the ṣaḍdarśanas or the six sys-tems of इन्दिअन् फिलोसोफ्य् is that of bheda (difference) and abheda (non-difference). Once a basic doctrine is evolved, it can then be applied to the relationship between the जीव (individual सोउल्) and परमात्मन् or ब्रह्मन् (the Supreme सोउल्).
Some of the schools of Vedānta like those of भास्कर (A.

) and निम्बार्क (12th century A.D.) propounded this doct-rine of bhedābheda (bhedābheda-वाद) between the जीव and ब्रह्मन्. There is both difference and identity between them, identity as pure चोन्स्चिओउस्नेस्स् and difference in powers and functions. Such bhedā-bheda is not inconceivable as can be seen in the relationship between गुण (quality) and guṇin (the substance possessing the quality) or between जाति (a genus or class) and vyakti (an individual belonging to that class).
See also ACINTYA-BHEDĀBHEDA SCHOOL.
